included_groups.rationale: Preserve the existing curated management allowlist. It is not the entire admin API: configuration writes, expiring clients and permission catalog/SoD remain explicit SDK debt. Selected HTML API-docs and SSE event methods remain compatible but do not prove streaming or HTML client support.
included_groups.exposure: Requires actual admin/gateway composition and each operation's stores or handlers; a documented or selected method does not mount a route.
included_groups.authentication: Admin bearer and admin:read/admin:write method scopes plus operation-specific governance; see the middleware, not merely OpenAPI security.
included_groups.defaults: admin_api gate omitted/true permits already wired routes; false hides gated routes. Optional stores, snapshots, replay and docs UI remain separately configured.
included_groups.licensing: Admin selection grants no commercial entitlement. Build profiles, tenant plans and deployment rights remain separate under docs/commercial-model.md.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve the existing OAuth/OIDC, login and credential-lifecycle generated methods; CIBA remains separately excluded. Selection is not complete flow or browser acceptance.
included_groups.exposure: Core SSO mounting plus conditional self-registration, password and registration stores/handlers; browser UIs remain external.
included_groups.authentication: Endpoint-specific client authentication, PKCE, credential or registration bearer contracts. An absent OpenAPI bearer declaration does not imply anonymous access.
included_groups.defaults: Existing endpoint/store/feature conditions are unchanged; generating a method neither enables a grant nor registers a client.
included_groups.licensing: No license policy is added by generation; artifact/profile, entitlement and deployment boundaries remain separate.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve selected FGA/ReBAC tuple, check and graph calls without treating the SDK as the authorization authority.
included_groups.exposure: ReBAC store and engine wiring determine the mounted product endpoints.
included_groups.authentication: Machine client-credentials and endpoint-specific scope/tenant checks; OpenAPI security is only the published declaration.
included_groups.defaults: No store/engine or policy is created by this inventory; feature/composition conditions remain with the server.
included_groups.licensing: Licensed feature-to-configuration mapping is operator-owned, not a runtime license check performed by this tool.

included_groups.rationale: Retain the historical mixed metadata/bootstrap/probe group, including the HTML check-session iframe. JSON-oriented generation is not proof of every selected media type or browser behavior.
included_groups.exposure: Discovery and JWKS reflect server state; setup, netpolicy, version preview and iframe have their own wiring/gates.
included_groups.authentication: Operation-specific: GET /api/v1/netpolicy/resolve-me is intentionally open current-request peer/host classification using r.RemoteAddr and r.Host, with no bearer authentication by this handler or AdminMiddleware. Managed /api/v1/netpolicy/classify (arbitrary inputs) and /api/v1/netpolicy/policies* instead require admin bearer with method scopes (GET admin:read, mutations admin:write) when AdminMiddleware is installed; SDK/custom compositions must supply equivalent protection, and stock admin-disabled wiring leaves these managed routes unauthenticated. Public metadata/probes and guarded bootstrap retain separate contracts. Missing OpenAPI security alone does not prove public access.
included_groups.defaults: setup_wizard.enabled defaults false; omitted feature gates do not construct missing dependencies. Other defaults are operation-specific.
included_groups.licensing: Discovery presence or SDK selection does not grant licensed features or establish production topology.

included_groups.rationale: Retain the existing federation metadata/trust-chain selection without claiming interoperability certification.
included_groups.exposure: Federation configuration, keys and endpoint wiring plus the live federation gate determine availability.
included_groups.authentication: Federation trust, signature, SSRF and endpoint validation are separate from any OpenAPI bearer declaration.
included_groups.defaults: Omitted/true gate permits configured routes only; it does not provision trust anchors, keys or subordinate stores.
included_groups.licensing: Federation grants map to precompiled modules/configuration under the commercial model; selection is not a license decision.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve selected subject device, permission, role, menu and activation/account projections; notifications remain explicitly unselected SDK debt.
included_groups.exposure: Subject-facing endpoints require their provider/store/activation wiring; commercial management is not mounted by this group.
included_groups.authentication: Current subject bearer and endpoint-specific client/tenant binding; activation tickets do not replace bearer authorization.
included_groups.defaults: Selection changes no self-service gate, device store or activation provider default.
included_groups.licensing: Account-context is a server-derived experience projection, not client authority or a grant to paid features.

included_groups.rationale: Retain the existing mesh external-authorization method; this is not a generic browser API or a new trusted-header contract.
included_groups.exposure: Requires the mesh/gateway deployment and its actual authorization wiring.
included_groups.authentication: Validates the intercepted bearer with DPoP/mTLS sender constraints and residency; derived X-Auth-* never trusts request identity. Trusted peer/proxy handling belongs to the mesh owner.
included_groups.defaults: No trusted proxy, peer identity or edge header policy is configured by generation.
included_groups.licensing: Artifact availability and deployment rights remain independent from this selected method.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve status/liveness/readiness clients without claiming metrics support, health correctness, capacity or availability SLA.
included_groups.exposure: Stock probes and runtime status depend on the HTTP composition; probes remain outside rate limiting.
included_groups.authentication: Operation-specific probe/status declarations; edge exposure must be configured separately.
included_groups.defaults: Readiness checks reflect configured dependencies; selection does not establish a healthy backend or production acceptance.
included_groups.licensing: A full binary or reachable probe is not an HA subscription or operational SLA.

included_groups.rationale: Retain the selected SCIM provisioning operations; generated request/response methods are not complete SCIM conformance acceptance.
included_groups.exposure: SCIM composition, stores and provisioning handlers must actually be installed.
included_groups.authentication: Stock fronts SCIM with AdminMiddleware bearer plus admin:read/admin:write and operation-specific tenant/subject rules; custom compositions must supply equivalent authorization.
included_groups.defaults: Stock SCIM requires admin auth enabled; Groups additionally needs scim.groups.enabled and a permissions provider. This coverage decision enables no route or permission.
included_groups.licensing: SCIM feature grants are mapped to precompiled modules/configuration by the deployment operator under the commercial model.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve the existing self-service subset; selected methods do not cover notification REST/SSE or supply a browser portal.
included_groups.exposure: Live self_service gate plus each password/MFA/identity/consent/privacy/org store and handler; branding is independently gated.
included_groups.authentication: Subject bearer, ownership and tenant checks, with endpoint-specific invitation/verification credentials; not every method shares one bearer rule.
included_groups.defaults: Omitted/true gates permit wired routes only; individual optional stores can leave routes unmounted.
included_groups.licensing: SDK calls grant no commercial entitlement, and external portal deployment remains separately owned.

included_groups.rationale: Retain selected Shared Signals metadata, receive and stream-management methods without inferring delivery/recovery or certification acceptance.
included_groups.exposure: CAEP/SSF receiver, transmitter and management wiring plus live feature gating determine availability.
included_groups.authentication: Receiver SET signature/issuer/audience/replay validation and management authorization are distinct from metadata and from OpenAPI bearer declarations.
included_groups.defaults: The caep gate cannot construct an unwired receiver; SDK selection changes no fail-closed or delivery policy.
included_groups.licensing: Module/configuration and commercial entitlements remain separate; no license enforcement is introduced here.

included_groups.rationale: Preserve the generated OIDC subject-profile read, not full OIDC or ID-token verification acceptance.
included_groups.exposure: OIDC endpoint wiring and live oidc gate determine reachability.
included_groups.authentication: Validated subject bearer with endpoint scope/claims rules; the server remains authoritative.
included_groups.defaults: Omitted/true gate permits the configured endpoint; no credential or session is created by generation.
included_groups.licensing: The generated operation is not a paid-feature grant or a publication decision.

included_groups.rationale: Retain existing WebAuthn ceremony methods without claiming browser/device acceptance or primary-passkey recovery.
included_groups.exposure: Authenticator/registrar stores and actual ceremony mounting are independently required.
included_groups.authentication: Ceremony challenge, origin/RP and session/user validation plus endpoint-specific bearer rules; no oracle distinction is added.
included_groups.defaults: Selection does not enable an authenticator, provision a credential or install a browser UI.
included_groups.licensing: Configured authenticator availability and commercial deployment rights remain independent from the allowlist.

excluded_groups.rationale: Retain the deliberate existing CIBA exclusion until a bounded end-to-end CIBA SDK contract is implemented and accepted; the server operation already exists.
excluded_groups.exposure: Live ciba gate is separate from CIBA store, authenticator/user resolution and delivery transport wiring.
excluded_groups.authentication: Confidential client authentication requires a non-empty secret (Basic takes precedence over body credentials) or a verified private_key_jwt assertion. Registered public clients with token_endpoint_auth_method="none" may supply client_id without a secret or assertion; this identifies the client, not proof of possession. Both paths enforce registered/active client, tenant, resource and scope checks; absent OpenAPI bearer security is not unrestricted anonymous access.
excluded_groups.defaults: Omitted/true ciba gate permits the route, which can return 501 without a CIBA store; gate false hides it. This inventory enables nothing.
excluded_groups.licensing: CIBA configuration and deployment/commercial rights remain with their owners; exclusion is not a license prohibition.

excluded_groups.rationale: Explicit generated-SDK coverage debt for existing JSON inbox and preference operations, not a claim that the server lacks notifications.
excluded_groups.exposure: Inbox/read needs NotificationStore; preference operations need NotificationPreferenceStore; all use the live self_service gate.
excluded_groups.authentication: Subject bearer with tenant/ownership checks; requests cannot select another subject's inbox.
excluded_groups.defaults: Stock notifications.enabled defaults false and BuildNotifications returns no options when disabled; selection does not wire stores.
excluded_groups.licensing: Notification product rights/quotas and platform notification wiring are distinct; no new free/paid or runtime license policy is inferred.

excluded_groups.rationale: SSE subscription, cancellation and reconnection are not modeled by a normal JSON return value; retain exclusion until a streaming contract is accepted.
excluded_groups.exposure: Requires inbox store AND notification broker, under the self_service gate.
excluded_groups.authentication: Subject bearer and subject-filtered events; it is not an unauthenticated event feed.
excluded_groups.defaults: notifications.enabled defaults false; stock enabled wiring supplies a broker, but embedders must wire it explicitly.
excluded_groups.licensing: SSE transport availability is not notification product entitlement or delivery SLA.

excluded_groups.rationale: Prometheus text exposition is not a supported JSON client result; this does not remove the existing metrics endpoint.
excluded_groups.exposure: Metrics handler and edge/network exposure belong to the operational composition.
excluded_groups.authentication: OpenAPI has no security declaration; it does not verify a deployment's edge protection or authorize external scraping.
excluded_groups.defaults: Existing metrics wiring and observability defaults are unchanged; no endpoint exposure is implied by this decision.
excluded_groups.licensing: Observability availability is not a production SLA or commercial entitlement decision.

excluded_groups.rationale: Existing JSON management operations are explicit SDK debt. Approval, reason, digest/CAS and canary governance deserve their own SDK acceptance, not an unreviewed bulk addition.
excluded_groups.exposure: Requires admin API wiring, a snapshot source AND config audit store; canary/atomic rollback have additional store/probe requirements.
excluded_groups.authentication: Admin bearer with admin:write, mandatory approve=true and reason; apply digest and optional expected-version/canary contracts remain authoritative.
excluded_groups.defaults: Absent required wiring leaves routes unmounted; canary is opt-in and does not change the live running configuration.
excluded_groups.licensing: Operator governance and commercial deployment rights remain independent; exclusion is not a licensing decision.

excluded_groups.rationale: The existing admin gateway/API query is explicit generated-SDK coverage debt, not an absent or unsupported server feature.
excluded_groups.exposure: Requires actual admin/gateway and client-store wiring.
excluded_groups.authentication: Admin bearer and admin:read plus the query's tenant/filter boundaries.
excluded_groups.defaults: Admin feature/dependency conditions remain unchanged; a documented query is not proof of default exposure.
excluded_groups.licensing: Client lifecycle governance does not acquire a commercial grant from either inclusion or exclusion.

excluded_groups.rationale: Existing resource catalog, static/dynamic separation-of-duty and session-role APIs are explicit SDK debt; preserve the selected role/assignment methods without claiming full permission coverage.
excluded_groups.exposure: Requires admin/gateway permission provider and the corresponding resource/conflict/session capabilities.
excluded_groups.authentication: Admin bearer with admin:read/admin:write, client/tenant bucket and session-role governance checks.
excluded_groups.defaults: Selection does not install a provider or expose unavailable optional capabilities; existing admin gates remain unchanged.
excluded_groups.licensing: Permission configuration and licensed grants remain operator/server concerns, not this inventory's decisions.

excluded_groups.rationale: Existing commercial management APIs belong to the separately deployed Billing/custom composition boundary, not the default generated SSO client. This is unselected SDK scope, not missing server functionality.
excluded_groups.exposure: snaplink-billing mounts commerce handlers with durable stores and a complete admin route contract; embedders must supply equivalent upstream authorization.
excluded_groups.authentication: Validated issuer/audience bearer plus exact admin:read/admin:write route contracts; financial mutations preserve tenant, idempotency and lifecycle rules.
excluded_groups.defaults: Not default stock sso-server routes. Separate Billing configuration and storage are required; no service is started by generation.
excluded_groups.licensing: Billing plans, subscriptions, entitlements and wallet facts are a separate commercial/data owner; no free/paid permission or production license is inferred.

excluded_groups.rationale: Purpose-specific out-of-process payment-adapter calls need their own client contract, not browser admin methods. Raw provider webhooks and secrets remain outside these normalized endpoints.
excluded_groups.exposure: Separate Billing composition explicitly installs payment routes with a required machine gate and PaymentSources resolver.
excluded_groups.authentication: Validated client-credentials identity shape, purpose-specific payment scopes and server-owned client/tenant/payment-provider binding. Path/body values cannot grant authority.
excluded_groups.defaults: Not mounted by default stock SSO; missing gate/resolver prevents payment route installation. Existing financial idempotency remains unchanged.
excluded_groups.licensing: The payment-adapter and Billing boundaries are separate deployments and do not grant a tenant plan or alter licensing policy.

excluded_groups.rationale: Usage append/reserve/commit/release and machine entitlement reads are a dedicated machine integration with binding/idempotency obligations, not general generated SSO-client calls.
excluded_groups.exposure: Separate Billing/custom composition needs usage ledger, entitlements and server-owned source resolver plus upstream RS middleware.
excluded_groups.authentication: Issuer/audience validated client-credentials identity, metering:write or billing:entitlement:read and enabled source binding. Tenant/source are server-derived, never selected by request data.
excluded_groups.defaults: No default stock SSO mounting; missing dependencies fail construction. Reservation and idempotency limits stay with the ledger owner.
excluded_groups.licensing: Usage facts and entitlement projections implement the existing commercial model; SDK omission neither disables billing nor grants limits.

excluded_groups.rationale: Internal monotonic commercial quota projection is a dedicated trusted machine ingress, not an endpoint to bulk-add to a general application SDK.
excluded_groups.exposure: Stock mounts only with projection_ingress.enabled and a projection-capable quota backend; audience and source registry are explicitly configured.
excluded_groups.authentication: Client-credentials identity, configured exact audience, tenant-quota:projection:write and exact enabled client_id/source_system server binding; body tenant_id grants no authority.
excluded_groups.defaults: Ingress is not enabled implicitly. Route enablement/backend/audience remain cold; source-only desired state may reload under the existing registry contract.
excluded_groups.licensing: Projects existing entitlements under docs/commercial-model.md; it is not a new runtime license decision or authorization to alter another tenant's quota.
